name: md any where
subtitle: Markdown, math and AI writing
promotional_text: Edit Markdown, preview equations, and export documents on iPhone and iPad. Optional agents use your configured service, with confirmation before each remote run.
description:
md any where is a Markdown and AI writing editor available on macOS, iPhone, and iPad. No md any where account is required to edit, preview, save, or export your work.

Writing and preview
• Multi-tab editing, find and replace, undo, and editing history
• Heading outlines, tables, task lists, and syntax highlighting
• Offline LaTeX rendering and a practical subset of flowchart syntax
• Touch layouts for iPhone and iPad, with keyboard and orientation support

Files and export
• Open, save, and share Markdown through the system Files interface
• Recover local drafts when you return to the app
• Export HTML, PDF, and standard DOCX documents
• Configure DOCX fonts, margins, spacing, and editable mathematical equations; complex formatting may vary by output and reader

Optional agents
Configure a compatible service endpoint, model, and API key for editing, proofreading, summaries, or multi-step workflows. All agents are disabled by default. Each remote run requires confirmation of its recipient and scope. Providers may charge for API usage and retain requests under their own policies. md any where does not include model credits, and agents are not required for local editing.

Ordinary editing, preview, and export run on your device. API keys are persisted in the system Keychain. External file providers and configured agent services process data according to their own policies.

md any where source code is available under the MIT License. Bundled third-party components retain their own licenses.

Three platforms and AI editors
The open-source project includes macOS, iPhone, and iPad versions. The macOS version connects to compatible AI editors such as Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor through MCP or CLI. This iPhone/iPad app provides built-in agent workflows, not desktop IDEs or the macOS command-line host. Use system file services to move documents across devices; the app does not operate its own cloud sync service.
review_notes:
md any where 1.0.0 (6) is a Markdown editor for iPhone and iPad. No md any where account, subscription or purchase is required for local editing, offline preview, Files integration, draft recovery or export. There are no ads or in-app purchases.

Review the local features by creating a document containing a heading, list, table and $x^2$, switching to preview, using the Document menu to save/export HTML, PDF or DOCX, and backgrounding/reopening the app to inspect draft recovery. The interface follows the system language and can be changed in Settings.

Optional AI is a bring-your-own-service client, disabled by default. The publisher does not operate an AI server, issue service accounts, provide model credits or embed an API key. In Document > Settings and Agents, users enter their own compatible endpoint, model and credential, save and enable the profile, select text and open Agent to run a writing task. API use is governed by the selected provider's account, regional, age and billing requirements. There is no publisher demo credential for this external service path. Please contact the review contact if additional access or evidence is required for this client architecture.

Every remote run names its destination and data scope and requires explicit consent; Cancel sends nothing. Credentials are kept in Keychain, requests go directly to the configured endpoint, and automatic HTTP redirects are rejected. Some actions send a selection/context; summaries and full-document workflows can send the entire document. The publisher collects no documents, credentials, analytics or diagnostic telemetry. Privacy labels disclose the built-in optional API integrations based on provider-retained content, account identifiers, usage and technical logs. These are provider-side practices, not a publisher backend. No third-party AI SDK, advertiser or analytics SDK is embedded. Users can change endpoints; the label does not assert identical behavior by every custom server. Please let us know if this BYOK architecture requires a different disclosure classification. Provider policies differ and may include model improvement. No advertising tracking is implemented.

The app has no public content feed, user-to-user messaging or unrestricted in-app web browsing. Its supplied content and writing templates contain no mature topics. Optional generated content depends on the user's task/provider; the app does not claim a universal moderation layer. It is a general writing utility, not a Kids-category app.

The macOS MCP/CLI helper and Finder extensions described in the project are not included in this iPhone/iPad binary. Documents can be transferred using system file providers; there is no publisher-operated cloud sync. Distribution is free and excludes mainland China. Release remains manual after approval.
